problem:
The fourth-degree Taylor polynomial of $f(x)$ about $x=0$ is given by

$$
{P}_{4}(x)=-1+2x-\frac{11}{4}{x}^{2}+\frac{5}{2}{x}^{3}+\frac{3}{8}{x}^{4}.
$$

What is ${f}^{″}(0)?$

${f}^{″}(0)=$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
The coefficient of ${x}^{2}$ is given by $\frac{{f}^{″}(0)}{2!}.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{f}^{″}(0)}{2!} & =-\frac{11}{4} \\ \frac{{f}^{″}(0)}{2} & =-\frac{11}{4} \\ {f}^{″}(0) & =-\frac{11}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
